title: EO 14399 Voter Data Request (California Secretary of State - Election Division)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: EO 14399 Voter Data Request (California Secretary of State - Election Division)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) All communications, letters, demands, instructions, and emails between United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (“USCIS”) agency officials, including but not limited to the USCIS’s Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate (“FDNS”), and state election officials regarding:
-- The implementation of Executive Order 14399 (“Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections”).
-- Development of a state citizenship list portal, including any records, including drafts, attachments, and implementing guidance, concerning the USCIS “Executive Order 14399 Implementation” memoranda directing the creation of infrastructure for state citizenship portals (June 8, 2026), https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053.151.1.pdf. 
-- Plans to transfer personally identifiable data to create state citizenship lists, including receipts showing data transfer between relevant agencies.
-- Implementation of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.” The “Unlawful Voter Initiative” refers to the initiative described in the “Disclosure Letter to Senator Padilla from Anonymous Whistleblower re: Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Direction to Identify ‘Unlawful Voters,’” (Sept 13, 2026), https://www.democrats.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/091326_-_senate_whistleblower_letter_dhs_uscis_combined_signedpdf.pdf. 

2) All memoranda of understanding (MOUs), data sharing agreements, or negotiations between state election officials and USCIS officials regarding granting federal agents access to personally identifiable data of state voters or the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.”

3) All log files, export or query counts, and metadata showing access of state voter data by USCIS personnel in searchable, machine-readable format, involving: time stamps, access metrics, confirmations of attestation statements (that the searcher is the voter or acting with the voter’s express authorization), search query parameters, pseudonymized user IDs, and system event codes. Remove personally identifiable information. 

4) Any internal complaints, alerts, incident investigations, audits, communications, reports, or notices regarding suspected violations of state election privacy laws relevant to the implementation of Executive Order 14399, the “Unlawful Voter Initiative,” and the creation of state citizenship lists. 

I am requesting these records for the time period of March 1, 2026 to the present.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michelle Du

communications.communication:
Hello,

The SD-LECC is in receipt of your request dated and received on August 11, 2026, requesting records pursuant to the California Public Records Act (CPRA).  Preliminarily, it must be stated that the SD-LECC is not a "public agency" within the meaning of the California Public Records Act.  It is a work location staffed with personnel from multiple local, state, and federal agencies working towards common operating goals, akin to a law enforcement "task force."  While a task force may, under certain circumstances, be considered a "public agency" within the meaning of the California Public Records Act and the Brown Act, those circumstances do not exist with regard to the SD-LECC.  Nevertheless, the SD-LECC, in the spirit of public disclosure and openness, is responding to the request as if the SD-LECC were a self-contained, distinct public agency. The SD-LECC will provide you with responsive documents by end of business on August 20, 2026, and if any records are withheld, applicable exemptions will be identified at that time.

Thank you,


Roy W. Frank

SD-LECC Director

San Diego Law Enforcement Coordination Center

***This email is being sent on behalf of Deputy Director Kristi Laughlin, SD-LECC Privacy Officer.***

To whom it may concern / Shawn Segal / MuckRock News

The SD-LECC is in receipt of your request dated and received on August 11, 2026, requesting records pursuant to the California Public Records Act (CPRA). Preliminarily, it must be stated that the SD-LECC is not a "public agency" within the meaning of the California Public Records Act. It is a work location staffed with personnel from multiple local, state, and federal agencies working towards common operating goals, akin to a law enforcement "task force." While a task force may, under certain circumstances, be considered a "public agency" within the meaning of the California Public Records Act and the Brown Act, those circumstances do not exist with regard to the SD-LECC. Nevertheless, the SD-LECC, in the spirit of public disclosure and openness, is responding to the request as if the SD-LECC were a self-contained, distinct public agency.

Requested information:

Emails between March 1, 2026 and August 10, 2026 between SD‑LECC and any of the following domains:
@anomalysix.com, @penlink.com, @cobwebs.com, @creativeradicals.com, @twosixtech.com, @venntel.com, @gravyanalytics.com, @verint.com

Any emails (regardless of domain) containing any of the following keywords in the subject or body: “Anomaly Six,” “Anomaly 6,” “Anomoly6,” “PenLink,” “Webloc,” “Creative Radicals,” “Two Six Technologies,” “Venntel,” “Gravy Analytics,” or “Unacast.”

After a diligent review, the SD-LECC has determined that no responsive emails exist for the listed domains or keywords with the following limited exceptions:

• PenLink – Identified in earlier correspondence, as well as in the current attachment.
• Venntel – One prior email mentioning “Venntel” was located. Identified and provided in previous communication.
• Anomaly 6 – One record referencing “Anomaly 6” exists; this record is being withheld with applicable exemptions.
The SD‑LECC has identified a record responsive to your request that is published under the Traffic Light Protocol (TLP:GREEN). OPE Email 2 Attachment – TLP – GREEN – DIGITAL EXHAUST GUIDE (FOR EXTERNAL PARTNERS – VERSION 5.0) Originating agency: OPE FBI, April 27, 2026.

This document contains sensitive information related to the privacy and security of law enforcement personnel data. Release of this material would reveal specific security risks, operational vulnerabilities, and protective methodologies used by law enforcement, which would compromise the safety of personnel.

Pursuant to California Government Code § 7922.000, the SD‑LECC is withholding this document in its entirety. The public interest served by nondisclosure clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure. Public release of TLP:GREEN information would undermine established confidentiality expectations, impede future intelligence‑sharing with trusted partners, and expose law enforcement personnel to heightened security threats. Maintaining the confidentiality of this material is essential to safeguarding sensitive law enforcement data and ensuring the continued protection of personnel and their families.

The SD-LECC has completed this request and has provided all responsive documents.

Sincerely,

SD-LECC Privacy Unit

communications.subject: Request for Clarification - PRR-2025-0631
communications.communication:
Dear Moe K. Clark, This correspondence is to update you on your public records request. You requested the following: - Any and all lists, spreadsheets or other organized datasets that detail potential or substantiated allegations of misconduct and/or impeached or impeachable testimony, created under Brady v. Maryland and/or Giglio v. United States. 

- Any and all records regarding substantiated allegations of misconduct or violations of internal department policy or criminal law by specific law enforcement officers. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. This email is to seek clarification of your request. Our request for clarification is as follows: All Washington Brady-Giglio list, formally known as Potential Impeachment Disclosure (PID) under RCW 10.93.180, are required to be maintained by each individual law enforcement agency and reported to their county’s Prosecuting Attorney Office (PAO) within 10 days of an incident occurring. See RCW 10.93.180: Protocol for potential impeachment disclosures. There are 39 county prosecutors’ offices in Washington, and one of our divisions currently has about eleven lists in their possession but they may be outdated at this current juncture, and we are interpreting your request to be seeking the most up to date list. Nonetheless, we are more than happy to produce the limited materials we have but, if you are looking for the most accurate information available, you may want to contact the county prosecutors’ offices. Please let us know right away, but not later than October 3, 2025, if you wish to receive the approximate 11 lists. In addition, we have the following questions regarding the records you are seeking: 1.  may we apply a timeframe to your request? such as 2025? or the last year? 2.  may we apply a specific law enforcement agency? such as Olympia, WA Police Department or the Thurston County Sheriff's Department? Please let us know right away, but not later than October 3, 2025. If we do not hear from you on or before this date, we will begin producing records in installments as they come available. Please note that installments are provided free of charge via Box for inspection and/or download. You will not need a Box account to access the records. If you have any questions, please contact me via email or at Office of the Attorney General, Public Records & Constituent Services, P.O. Box 40100, Olympia, WA 98504-0100. Thank you. Sincerely,

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Texas Public Information Act, Tex. Gov't Code Chapter 552, I request copies of the following records held by this office, in any format (email and all attachments thereto, letters, memoranda, text messages, meeting calendars or logs, call logs, or notes):

- All communications, in either direction, between this office and any of the following individuals or organizations, regarding S.R. 438 (2009), S.B. 1634 (2025), or Lipan Apache tribal recognition generally, INCLUDING ALL ATTACHMENTS to any such communication (PDFs, scanned documents, images, or any other file type):

          - Individuals: Bernard F. Barcena Jr., Robert Soto, Lucille Contreras, Daniel Castro Romero Jr., Richard A. Gonzalez, Mandy/Mande Gonzales Davalos, Christina Hernandez, Margo Tamez, Eloisa Garcia Tamez, or any staff/representative acting on their behalf
          - Organizations: Lipan Apache Tribe of Texas, Lipan Apache Band of Texas, Texas Tribal Buffalo Project, Lipan Apache Tribe of Brackettville Texas, Lipan Apache Women Defense / LAW Defense, People of La Junta for Preservation
          - Any email address ending in: @lipanapachetribe.gov, @lipanapachetribe.org, @texastribalbuffaloproject.org, @lipanapachetribeofbrackettvilletexas.org, or @peopleoflajunta.org

- All records reflecting any meeting, call, or in-person contact between this office and any of the individuals or organizations listed above, including calendar entries, visitor logs, or scheduling records.

- Any documents, exhibits, proof of tribal status, genealogical records, organizational filings (articles of incorporation, IRS determination letters, bylaws), letters of support, or other supporting materials submitted to this office by any of the individuals or organizations listed above — whether submitted by email, mail, in person, or through any other channel, and whether or not attached to a specific tracked communication.

- Any internal memoranda, staff analysis, or briefing materials prepared regarding S.R. 438 or S.B. 1634, excluding only material specifically exempted as a draft or working paper under § 552.106.

Requested date range: March 1, 2009 through present.

I recognize this office may consider withholding certain records under Tex. Gov't Code §§ 306.003–306.004. State recognition of a tribe carries direct federal consequences under existing law, including the U.S. Small Business Administration's 8(a) Business Development program, which applies the label of "socially disadvantaged" status to enrolled members of state-recognized tribes, and the Indian Arts and Crafts Act of 1990 (18 U.S.C. § 1159), which governs who may lawfully market goods as authentic Native American-made. A separate GAO report (GAO-12-348, 2012) specifically points to federal funding the Lipan Apache have already received. As a reporter, this is a matter of genuine public interest under § 306.004(a)(3), not merely a private legislative matter.

I am requesting these records be produced in electronic format where available. If any portion of this request is denied or withheld, please cite the specific statutory exception relied upon for each withheld item, consistent with § 552.301. If costs are expected to exceed $40, please provide a written cost estimate before proceeding, per my rights under the Act.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Tristan Ahtone

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Request for Lexipol correspondence (Chico Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All records, between the Department and the company Lexipol  (lexipol.com) or its representatives that contain any references to “military equipment” or “AB 481”, including documents, emails and attachments, texts, spreadsheets, recordings, memoranda, and other materials, from July 1, 2024 to the present. 

Records on the Department’s web site indicate that it has used Lexipol templates for at least some policies. 

To assist with the prompt release of responsive material, I ask that you make records available to me as you locate them, rather than waiting until all responsive records have been collected and copied.
 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

John Lindsay-Poland

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: DOD self-identified trans records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Reports, policy memos, forms, form responses, emails, text messages, separation documents and other records regarding active-duty and reserve forces service members who have been diagnosed with or “exhibit symptoms consistent with” gender dysphoria and identified themselves for voluntary separation. I request records both from the Department of Defense connected to the separations, guiding policy and their requirements under Executive Order 14183, as well as records regarding individual service members' self-identification and voluntary separation. 

I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

I request a complete waiver of all search and duplication fees. If my request for a waiver is denied, I request that I be considered a member of the news media for fee purposes. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, processed by a representative of the news media/press and is made in the process of news gathering and not for commercial usage. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request.

Under the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016, agencies must adopt a presumption of disclosure, withholding information “only if . . . disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption” or “disclosure is prohibited by law.”

The FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 also amended the FOIA as follows (5 USC 552(a)(8)):

(A) An agency shall—
(i) withhold information under this section only if—
(I) the agency reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption described in subsection (b); or
(II) disclosure is prohibited by law; and
(ii) (I) consider whether partial disclosure of information is possible whenever the agency determines that a full disclosure of a requested record is not possible; and
(II) take reasonable steps necessary to segregate and release nonexempt information. . .

In the event some portions of the requested records are properly exempt from disclosure, please disclose any reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of the requested records. If it is your position that a document contains non-exempt segments, but that those non-exempt segments are so dispersed throughout the document as to make segregation impossible, please state what portion of the document is non-exempt, and how the material is dispersed throughout the document. Claims of nonsegregability must be made with the same degree of detail as required for claims of exemptions in a Vaughn index. If a request is denied in whole, please state specifically that it is not reasonable to segregate portions of the record for release.

Further, “the withholding agency must supply ‘a relatively detailed justification, specifically identifying the reasons why a particular exemption is relevant and correlating those claims with the particular part of a withheld document to which they apply.’”

In addition, I ask that your agency exercise its discretion to release records which may be technically exempt, but where withholding serves no important public interest.

If a portion of the responsive records become available before the entire request is complete, I respectfully request that the department provide records on a rolling basis.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ileana Garnand

communications.communication:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All messages sent or received by Sacramento Sheriffs Office official instagram pages between January 1st, 2025 to June 27th 2025.

Original JPG. files, including the meta data, of all images posted on the Sacramento Sheriffs Instagram Profile between January 1st, 2025 to June 27th 2025.

All screenshots, taken by any agent of the Sacramento Sheriffs Department, that were posted onto Sacramento Sheriffs Office Instagram Page, on June 19th 2025.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

title: Public IT Configuration and Policy Data on breached account containing  MnCHOICES reports

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Public IT Configuration and Policy Data on breached account containing  MnCHOICES reports
communications.communication:
Aitkin County Data Practices Compliance Official

Subject: MGDPA Request: Public IT Configuration and Policy Data

Statutory Framework and ADA Accommodation Request
Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act (Minn. Stat. Chapter 13), I am requesting access to the public government data listed below.

Under Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. §§ 12131-12165) and the MGDPA, I have a statutory right to inspect this data at no charge. Due to the volume and technical complexity of the requested materials, an at-length, in-person inspection is not feasible without a customized environment. Therefore, as a reasonable accommodation, I request to inspect these records in their original electronic format via a secure remote connection.

To eliminate the administrative burden on your agency to facilitate a live remote inspection, I will accept digital copies of the requested records delivered via email at no cost. Delivery of these digital copies fully satisfies this ADA accommodation request.

There should be no charge for this request. If you determine Aitkin County would like to charge for this request beyond the cost of the storage medium, or if the cost of storage of the data segregated for inspection would exceed $50 (e.g., 2TB at commercial pricing), do not proceed without contacting me.

Data Requested
I am requesting the following strictly public administrative IT records regarding the environment surrounding the data security incident discovered on April 8, 2026:

Account Configuration: IT administrative records, provisioning logs, or server configurations indicating whether the compromised email account utilized to store the MnCHOICES report was assigned to a single individual user or configured as a shared distribution list/group inbox.

Retention Policies: The active Aitkin County Records Retention Schedule and Email Management Policy in effect during April 2026.

Parameters
This request explicitly excludes any Private Data on Individuals. I am requesting only the public IT configurations and administrative policies. If you determine any portion of this request encompasses classified data, you must provide the specific statutory citation authorizing the redaction or denial, as required by Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(f).

Appendix: Technical Search and Retrieval Parameters
To facilitate compliance and limit the administrative burden on your IT department, please route the following parameter to the Microsoft 365/Exchange Administrator:

For Item 1 (Account Configuration): Within the Exchange Admin Center (EAC), navigate to Recipients -> Mailboxes. Mr. Jonathon Murray,



Thank you for your patience and your questions. It’s our understanding that the DHS fields potentially affected were: FormID, an ID to designate the person, “personname,” a “PMI,” formtype, “type,” State, a modified date, last modified by (whom), org, and locations.



In terms of your other questions, they may be better directed to DHS. However, I do want you to know some additional information we have. Typically, DHS would pull and provide us our individual county data. In this instance, though we did not request it (or, frankly, know it was sent), DHS filtered the spreadsheet and sent the filtered version of the spreadsheet to us, but containing information from all 87 Counties. Upon receipt, with the filtering involved, the recipient at our county did not know there was other out-of-county information included. That email was deleted shortly after receipt. Only in the wake of this incident did a forensic analyst locate the filtered spreadsheet in the user’s Deleted items folder. We have since modified our settings as to Deleted Items folders. We have no evidence of any leak of any of this data. We have no evidence of any of this information being misused in any way.



I would also point out that, as noted in the letter you received from DHS, they stopped transmitting MnCHOICES data in June 2025, which was approximately a year before the incident.

title: CVISS Minutes and LexisNexis/Accurint Data Sharing

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CVISS Minutes and LexisNexis/Accurint Data Sharing
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. The current Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) governing the Central Valley Information Sharing System (CVISS), including all participating agency joinder agreements and the full list of current member agencies.

2. CVISS Meeting minutes for 2025 and 2026 CVISS meetings. 

3. All current contracts, addendums, amendments, and schedules signed with LexisNexis (aka RELX / LexisNexis Risk Management / Accurint). This includes The 'Accurint Virtual Crime Center / Accurint Crime Analysis / LexisNexis Community Crime Map / AVCC XML Addendum' or 'PSDEX Addendum' executed by the Sacramento County Sheriff's Office as Lead Agency for the CVISS consortium, including all exhibits and schedules (e.g. Schedule A).

4. Any 'AVCC XML / PSDEX Addendum' or 'Member Agency Addendum and Joinder' executed by any CVISS member agency in your possession.

5) Agency Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing

Context: We understand that CVISS moved to Accurint to share data among CVISS members. We are seeking to understand whether Sacramento County Sheriff and other CVISS members share data with agencies beyond the consortium (PSDEX / National Database) or restricts data sharing to CVISS members only.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Air Force support for 2021 movie "Don't Look Up"
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents pertaining to collaboration between the US Air Force and the production of the 2021 film "Don' Look Up," directed by Adam McKay. I request any and all documents pertaining to US Air Force involvement with the production of "Don't Look Up." Such documents may include but should not be limited to: script notes; production assistance agreements; photographs; and all records of communications between employees of US Air Force and members of the cast, crew, and production company of "Don't Look Up," including memos, notes of meetings and conference calls, emails, and other forms of communication.

"Don't Look Up" appears on a list of Air Force-supported productions released to me via FOIA. That list is attached to this request. 

I am the Director of Research Operations at a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization called The Decoding Culture Foundation. These documents will be used for public education and research purposes. I therefore request a waiver of all fees that may otherwise apply. Attached is a document with organization letterhead confirming my position, as well as the organization's 501(c)(3) application and approval form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Carollo

1) All MOUs, contracts, addendums, or other legal documents signed by your agency and LexisNexis (and subsidiaries, including LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Accurint, AVCC, PSDEX, etc.). This may include (but is not limited to) a LexisNexis Consortium Sub-Agency Addendum, Schedule A, or other agreements.
2) Any MOUs or other agreements between your agency and CVISS or Sacramento County Sheriff related to sharing RMS/CAD data.
3) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing

We are seeking to understand whether your agency and other CVISS members share contributed data with agencies beyond the consortium (e.g., the Public Safety Data Exchange / PSDEX national database), or whether data sharing is restricted to CVISS members only. Often LexisNexis Sub-Agency Addendums allow agencies to choose whether they share nationally or only within the consortium - we seek to understand what your agency chose to do.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request #26-1955
communications.communication:
Hi Anna,

I am looking for documents from 1/1/2022 through present - with a few caveats that will hopefully make the search easier:
A) I only need one copy of each document type. If you've signed a few contracts with LexisNexis over the years, I only need the most recent. 
B) For request #1, the most important document I am looking for is titled "AVCC XML Addendum." It's typically attached to a Schedule A and Master Service Agreement (MSA) which I'd love as well, but the AVCC XML Addendum is what dictates whether your data is shared nationally or only with consortium members - and that's the question we're trying to answer. 
C) For #2, if this yields dozens of results, we only need a few of the most recent examples - not every single one. Some consortiums sign new ones each year and I don't need the entire history - just the most recent several. 
D) Same with #3 - we're only looking for most recent info. If you cannot find the screenshot, this alternative export will also work:  An export of what data you share with CCM and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with (CCM only, or also other law enforcement agencies?) [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]

Thank you,
Shawn

title: LexisNexis Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) PSDEX Data Sharing Agreement (Austin Police Department)

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: LexisNexis Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) PSDEX Data Sharing Agreement (Austin Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is focused on Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) and Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEX), both are products of LexisNexis Risk Solutions (LNRS / RELX). We are making this request because we found evidence that your agency likely uses, has access to, or contributes data to AVCC (directly or indirectly). If your agency has no relationship with these products, please tell us so.

We are seeking records that indicate whether your agency contributes data to AVCC/PSDEX, and if so, what other agencies have access to that data. 
--
We are requesting the following records:
1) All signed contracts, addendums, amendments, or agreements between your agency and LexisNexis that are currently in effect or were in effect at any point between 1/1/2020 and the date this request is fulfilled.  
[CONTEXT] Common documents include "AVCC XML Addendum" / "Schedule A" / "Master Terms & Conditions" / "sub-agency agreements" / "joinder agreements" or other similar agreements. If your agency contributes data or gets AVCC access through a consortium or fusion center, please include the MOU or similar agreement outlining that AVCC relationship. 
2) AVCC Usage Logs. 
 - 2.A) If your agency shares data with AVCC/PSDEX, please provide query logs of who has accessed your agency's data and what reason/case number they provided while searching your agency's records. We understand some of these reports are generated by LexisNexis rather than stored locally; please include any such report your agency has received or can obtain. Please provide in CSV or XLSX format where available. If you are unable to see logs of how your agency's data is used by other agencies within AVCC, please indicate so. 
3) AVCC Configuration:
 - 3.A) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing 
 - 3.B) Configuration Explainer Documents: Typically documents with details on what data LexisNexis recommends that you contribute, and what they recommend you exclude. Sometimes this may be called "FAQs and FYIs for Exclusions", or may include integration suggestions for an interface with your RMS/JMS/CAD systems.

Sincerely, 

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act Request: Public Records Request: Flock audits (Carlsbad Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Organization Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2023, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

2. Network Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2023, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

3. Event Log in Flock
The Flock Safety Event Log for the time period of January 1, 2023, to the date this request is processed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

e

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications) (Petaluma Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I request the following records concerning any products, services, platforms, sensors, or data feeds of the following categories, whether currently used, previously used, piloted, trialed, or formally considered by this agency, for the period January 1, 2020 through July 6, 2026:

Automated license plate reader ("ALPR") and connected-camera systems — including but not limited to Flock Safety (Flock Group Inc.), Motorola Solutions / Vigilant Solutions (LEARN, PlateSearch), Genetec (AutoVu), Axon / Fusus, Rekor, Leonardo/ELSAG, Neology, and Digital Recognition Network (DRN);
Data-integration, analytics, and "real-time crime center" (RTCC) / "real-time awareness center" (RTAC) platforms — including but not limited to Peregrine Technologies (peregrine.io), Palantir, Fusus (Axon), SoundThinking, and any comparable platform that aggregates, links, or searches across agency data sources; and
Any product beyond ALPR cameras offered by the above vendors (e.g., Flock's Condor PTZ video, FlockOS, Nova, or other data-intelligence products; Peregrine's data-integration or AI/"safety flagging" modules).

Where a term below refers to a Flock-specific feature (e.g., "Organization Audit"), please read it to also request the equivalent record in any other vendor's system.
1. Contracts and procurement. All contracts, master services agreements, order forms, amendments, renewals, statements of work, quotes, proposals, purchase orders, invoices, and payment records with any vendor identified above, including any data-processing addenda / data-processing agreements (DPAs), memoranda of understanding (MOUs), and any competitive-bid waivers or sole-source justifications.
2. Vendor communications. All communications (email, text/SMS, letters, meeting notes, calendar invitations) between agency personnel and representatives of any vendor identified above (including the vendor's @flocksafety.com, @peregrine.io, or equivalent domains), concerning procurement, deployment, configuration, camera or sensor siting, pilot / early-access / free-trial programs, and any product beyond ALPR cameras.
3. Search and audit logs. The complete audit/usage logs showing each search or query, including — for Flock — the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs (Flock Insights dashboard), and — for any RTCC / data-integration platform (e.g., Peregrine) — the user access and query logs. For each entry, please include all available metadata fields, e.g.: record ID, user name, organization/agency name, date/time of search, license plate or query terms, stated reason, case number, camera count, time frame searched, filters, search type, and any text/AI prompt. Please export in the system's native machine-readable format (CSV/XLSX), not as a PDF printout, and do not strip metadata fields.
4. Hotlist and NCIC configuration (commonly the most important item). Records sufficient to show the full hotlist configuration of any ALPR system, including a screenshot, screen capture, printout, or CSV of the hotlists the agency subscribes to. This specifically includes which FBI NCIC "topics" are enabled and, in particular, whether the "Immigration Violator" file / topic is enabled, and the date any such topic was enabled or disabled. Also include any custom hotlists created by the agency.
5. Data sharing and external / federal access. A list of all external entities with which data is shared or from which it is received, and the settings governing that sharing, including:

The agency's Flock network-sharing settings, and whether "National Lookup" and/or statewide lookup are enabled, with the dates access was granted, modified, or revoked;
All external agencies that can access this agency's data, and all agencies whose data this agency can access, with dates;
Specifically, any access by or sharing with federal agencies — ICE, CBP, HSI, ATF, FBI, DHS — including records of searches those agencies (or other agencies on their behalf) ran against this agency's data;
All MOUs, data-sharing agreements, and network-participation terms (e.g., with a fusion center such as NCRIC), and any restrictions placed on downstream use or re-dissemination.

6. California ALPR statutory records (SB 34 and amendments).

The record of access required by Civil Code § 1798.90.52;
The agency's current ALPR usage and privacy policy required by Civil Code § 1798.90.51 (and, if the agency is an ALPR end-user, its policy under § 1798.90.53);
The results of the annual audit of ALPR searches for compliance with the usage/privacy policy (Civil Code § 1798.90.53), including any assessment of whether non-hotlist data was purged within 30 days of collection;
Any records concerning use of ALPR for immigration-enforcement geolocation or retention beyond 30 days (see Civ. Code § 1798.90.5 et seq., as amended).

7. Camera / sensor deployment and locations. Records sufficient to show the number, type, and locations of all cameras or sensors installed in the jurisdiction (fixed ALPR, mobile ALPR, PTZ/video, gunshot-detection, or other), their installation dates, and any encroachment, right-of-way, or other permits issued for their installation.
8. Data sources integrated into any data-integration / RTCC platform. For any platform identified above (e.g., Peregrine), a list of all data sources, feeds, and databases integrated into or accessible through the platform — for example computer-aided dispatch (CAD), records management systems (RMS), body-worn and in-car camera footage, fixed/traffic/school cameras, ALPR data, jail/booking data, DMV or state databases, and any third-party or commercial data sources — together with any system-configuration or data-source inventory documents.
9. Retention, governance, and training. Records reflecting data-retention periods and deletion practices, access controls (who is authorized to search and what approvals are required), prohibited uses, training materials, and internal policies, standard operating procedures, directives, or general orders governing use of any system identified above.
10. Misuse, breaches, and oversight. Any audits, reports, internal-affairs records, complaints, disciplinary records, or communications concerning suspected or confirmed misuse of any system (including searches for personal, immigration, or reproductive-health-related reasons), and any records of data breaches or security incidents involving the data.
11. Surveillance-use policy and impact reports. Any Surveillance Use Policy, Surveillance Impact Report, Privacy Impact Assessment / Data Protection Impact Assessment, or comparable document required by any applicable local surveillance-oversight ordinance, relating to ALPR, RTCC, or data-integration technology generally or to a specific vendor.
12. Governing-body review. Staff reports, resolutions, meeting agendas, minutes, and presentations to the city council / board of supervisors / oversight body concerning approval, funding, or renewal of any contract identified above.
13. Confirmation of non-use. If the agency has never used, piloted, or contracted for any ALPR, connected-camera, RTCC, or data-integration system of the kind described above, please confirm that in writing.

Format, preservation, and processing

Machine-readable format. Please provide records in their original electronic, machine-readable format with metadata intact (Gov. Code § 7922.570); spreadsheets and logs as CSV/XLSX, not PDF printouts.
Preservation. Because some responsive records (particularly ALPR search/audit logs) may be subject to short retention or automatic deletion, I request that the agency preserve all responsive records — and suspend any automatic purge of responsive audit logs — pending completion of this request.
Segregability and exemption log. If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify each record and the specific exemption claimed (Gov. Code § 7922.540), and release all reasonably segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525). Data describing how the system operates and is used — as distinct from information about a specific individual — is generally not exempt investigative material (see ACLU of S. Cal. v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032). Personal information may be redacted while still disclosing system-level records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

Releasing such details would reasonably be expected to compromise the effectiveness of those techniques by enabling individuals to evade detection or target the equipment for tampering or vandalism. The public interest served by withholding precise LPR deployment information, namely preserving the effectiveness and security of law enforcement tools and protecting public safety, clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure. It is reasonable to assert that the public has a strong and compelling interest in ensuring law enforcement surveillance systems operate effectively to promote public safety and that the disclosure of all ALPR camera locations in one record, would materially impair the integrity and effectiveness of the system by revealing the scope, placement, and coverage of surveillance infrastructure. Public oversight of the City’s LPR program is adequately served through the disclosure of the Police Department’s policy regulating its usage and data-retention policies, which are publicly available pursuant to Civil Code section 1798.90.5 et seq., without revealing sensitive operational details. Personal Information Exemption With respect to records containing personal information of Petaluma community members, the City has determined that certain details are exempt from disclosure under the catchall exemption set forth in Government Code section 7922.000 (formerly section 6255 of the Public Records Act). This provision authorizes a public agency to withhold a public record if it determines that “on the facts of the particular case, the public interest served by not disclosing the record clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure of the record.” The responsive records will be made available; however, names, addresses, email addresses and telephone numbers will be redacted. Disclosure of this personal information would not meaningfully contribute to the public’s understanding of how the City performs its duties—such as enforcing provisions of the Petaluma Municipal Code. Instead, public disclosure of such information could chill participation in City programs, discourage residents from reporting code violations, and impair the City’s ability to effectively enforce its laws. The California courts have recognized this balancing of interests in similar contexts. In City of San Jose v. Superior Court (1999) 74 Cal.App.4th 1008, the court upheld the withholding of personal contact information of complainants on the ground that disclosure could deter citizens from interacting with local government and frustrate legitimate enforcement efforts. Accordingly, the City has determined that the public interest in protecting the privacy of community members clearly outweighs any public interest in disclosure of the redacted information. For this reason, and pursuant to Government Code section 7922.000, this portion of your request is respectfully denied or redacted. The City has and will produce non-exempt, responsive records on a rolling basis as its review progresses. The next estimated production date is Monday July 27, 2026. title: Law Enforcement Equitable Sharing Request Information

communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: Law Enforcement Equitable Sharing Request Information
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

• A copy of all TDF-92 "Request for Transfer of Property Seized/Forfeited by a Treasury Forfeiture Fund Participating Agency" submissions for the period Jan. 1, 2023 through Sept. 21, 2026. A blank version of the form can be found at https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/246/Seized-2011-Property-Form-TD-F-92-22-46-OMB-1505-0152.pdf
• A copy of all Equitable Sharing Request Forms (DAG-71) submitted by this agency to the U.S. Department of Justice for the period Jan. 1, 2023 through Sept. 21, 2026. A blank version of the form can be found at https://www.justice.gov/file/485791/dl.
• A copy of all annual Equitable Sharing Agreement and Certification submissions for the period Jan. 1, 2023 through Sept 21, 2026. A blank version of the form can be found at https://www.justice.gov/criminal/media/1446466/dl?inline
• Any spreadsheet, index, or other umbrella document maintained by this agency that reflects equitable sharing requests made by this agency for the period Jan. 1, 2023 through Sept 21, 2026. Please include all available segregable information, including the nature of each request, the monetary value of each asset, and the final disposition of the request (i.e. was the request successful or not). 

This request is being made by a journalistic researcher. It is being made for research purposes, not commercial ones. Please assess fees in accordance with provisions for media requesters. In the event that this agency decides to charge this requester fees not to exceed the actual cost of reproducing the records, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request.

Please fulfill this request electronically, preferably by e-mail attachment, if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within the statutorily-mandated timeframe. 

Sincerely, 

Patrick File

Dear Requester, 
Attached are your requested records pertaining to request, records pertaining to 2023-9410. 
Certain information has been redacted from the records under Exemption 6 (personal privacy information). In determining to withhold such information, FDA considered 5 USC 552(a)(8)(i), when applicable, and whether FDA reasonably foresees that disclosure of such information would harm an interest protected by the relevant exemption(s) and whether disclosure is prohibited by law. 
This now closes your request with the agency. 
In accordance with 45 CFR § 5.61 and 21 CFR § 20.41(b)(5), you have the right to appeal this determination. Your appeal should clearly identify the agency determination that is being appealed. It would be helpful if you provide specific reasons explaining why you believe the agency's adverse determination should be reconsidered. By filing an appeal, you preserve your rights under FOIA and give the agency a chance to review and reconsider your request and the agency’s decision. Your appeal must be mailed within 90 days from the date of this response, to: Director, Office of Management and Enterprise Services, U.S. Food & Drug Administration, 5630 Fishers Lane, Room 1050, Rockville, MD 20857, or emailed within 90 days from the date of this response to FDAFOIA@fda.hhs.gov. Please clearly mark both the envelope and your letter “FDA Freedom of Information Act Appeal.” Items arriving or delivered after 5 p.m. Eastern Time will be deemed received on the next workday. (mailto:FDAFOIA@fda.hhs.gov) 
If you would like to discuss our response before filing an appeal to attempt to resolve your dispute without going through the appeals process, please contact FOI-OC-Group@fda.hhs.gov. (mailto:FOI-OC-Group@fda.hhs.gov)

If you are unable to resolve your FOIA dispute through our FOIA Public Liaison, the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS), the Federal FOIA Ombudsman’s office, offers mediation services to help resolve disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies.

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Audit Logs Dunwoody October - December 2024
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Copies of all audit logs, search logs, or usage reports related to your agency's use of Flock "ALPR" systems for the period October 1, 2024 through December 31, 2024. This includes but is not limited to the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs available in the Flock software's "Insights" section, showing records of license plate searches performed by agency personnel, timestamps of searches, user identification information (names, badge numbers, or user IDs), and any associated case numbers or investigation references.

Please provide records in their original electronic format (CSV, Excel, or similar).

To the extent any portion of these records is claimed exempt under the Open Records Act, I request that the exemption be applied at the field or column level rather than by withholding entire logs, consistent with the segregability requirement of O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1)(A). If a specific field (such as the free-text search justification field) is withheld, please identify which field and the specific statutory basis for withholding it.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

Subject: EXPEDITED FOIA DEMAND: Hazard Assessments & FEMA Region 3 Communications (1488-1500 Morris Rd SE)

To the FOIA Officers and Executive Leadership of D.C. HSEMA and DOEE:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-532), I am formally demanding the immediate release of the following public records pertaining to the active 25-foot landslide, federal MS4 infrastructure failure, and compromised public canopy located within the 1488 to 1500 block of Morris Rd SE.

This request specifically encompasses, but is not limited to, the following mandatory disclosures:

1. FEMA Communications:
All correspondence, emails, memorandums, and official requests sent from D.C. HSEMA, DOEE, or the Mayor's Office to FEMA Region 3 regarding the life-safety hazard and structural collapse at this specific location.

2. Hazard Mitigation Assessments:
All internal documents, Pre-Disaster Mitigation (PDM) funding evaluations, and structural assessments conducted by DOEE or HSEMA concerning the active landslide at 1488-1490 Morris Rd SE.

3. DDOT Interagency Briefings:
Any internal memos, briefings, risk assessments, or damage reports provided by the District Department of Transportation (DDOT) to HSEMA or DOEE regarding this site, including any directives attempting to classify, contain, or dismiss this multi-million dollar infrastructure failure without federal intervention.

Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full waiver of all search, review, and duplication fees. communications.subject: RE: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request #F26-729
communications.communication:
Hello,

I’ve inquired with the Police Services Bureau and the City of Wyoming does not have mobile trailer units as described in your recent follow up email. Therefore, the FOIA response provided on 8/31/2026 would not include records that are not maintained or possessed by our department.

The two cameras you may be referring to are the Falcon Flex cameras (portable), which were included in the FOIA response provided on 8/31/2026. According to the Police Services Bureau, these are the same type of cameras as those permanently affixed to poles and operate in the same manner. The department has the ability to deploy and set up the Falcon Flex cameras as needed.

The slides used in the City Commission meeting can be found in your FOIA response F26-825 sent on 9/15/2026.

If you have any further questions related to the FOIA response F26-729 documents, my contact information can be found below.

Monzerrat Perez

- Billings, invoices, and records of payment made pursuant to the contract.
- Monthly records on the average daily population and average length of detention of people detained in ICE custody at the jail.
- Complaints or grievances filed by people detained in ICE custody at the jail.

title: Department of Defense support for TV series "Did They Fix That?"

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Department of Defense support for TV series "Did They Fix That?"
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any documents pertaining to collaboration between the Department of Defense (DoD) and the production of the TV series "Did They Fix That?" (2023-). Such documents may include but should not be limited to: script notes; production assistance agreements; and all records of communications between employees of DoD and members of the cast, crew, and production company of "Did They Fix That?," including memos, notes of meetings and conference calls, emails, and other forms of communication.

"Did They Fix That?" appears on a list of DoD entertainment industry collaborations released to me through FOIA. The list is attached to this request.

I am the Director of Research Operations at a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization called The Decoding Culture Foundation as well as the editor-in-chief and a contributor to a research magazine published by said foundation titled "Cultural Engineering Studies." These documents will be used for public education and research purposes. I therefore request a waiver of all fees that may otherwise apply. Attached is a document with organization letterhead confirming my position, as well as the organization's 501(c)(3) application and approval form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Carollo

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Request: Zbigniew Brzezinski
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act.  I hereby request the following records:

Records relating to or mentioning Zbigniew Kazimierz Brzezinski AKA Zbigniew Kazimierz Brzeziński, March 28, 1928 – May 26, 2017. He was a Polish-American diplomat and political scientist. He served as a counselor to President Lyndon B. Johnson from 1966 to 1968 and was President Jimmy Carter's National Security Advisor from 1977 to 1981. Brzezinski belonged to the realist school of international relations, standing in the geopolitical tradition of Halford Mackinder and Nicholas J. Spykman. See the attached obituary for proof of death.

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or attachments. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

I am a member of the news media and request classification as such. I have previously written about the government and its activities for AND Magazine, MuckRock and Glomar Disclosure and have an open arrangement with each. My articles have been widely read, with some reaching over 100,000 readers. As such, as I have a reasonable expectation of publication and my editorial and writing skills are well established. In addition, I discuss and comment on the files online and make them available through the non-profit Internet Archive, disseminating them to a large audience. While my research is not limited to this, a great deal of it, including this, focuses on the activities and attitudes of the government itself. As such, it is not necessary for me to demonstrate the relevance of this particular subject in advance. Additionally, case law states that “proof of the ability to disseminate the released information to a broad cross-section of the public is not required.” Judicial Watch, Inc. v. Dep’t of Justice, 365 F.3d 1108, 1126 (D.C. Cir. 2004); see Carney v. U.S. Dep’t of Justice, 19 F.3d 807, 814-15 (2d Cir. 1994). Further, courts have held that "qualified because it also had “firm” plans to “publish a number of . . . ‘document sets’” concerning United States foreign and national security policy." Under this criteria, as well, I qualify as a member of the news media. Additionally, courts have held that the news media status "focuses on the nature of the requester, not its request. The provision requires that the request be “made by” a representative of the news media. Id. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(II). A newspaper reporter, for example, is a representative of the news media regardless of how much interest there is in the story for which he or she is requesting information." As such, the details of the request itself are moot for the purposes of determining the appropriate fee category. As such, my primary purpose is to inform about government activities by reporting on it and making the raw data available and I therefore request that fees be waived.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.


Sincerely,

M Best

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents mentioning Murray Bookchin (January 14, 1921 – July 30, 2006) - political philosopher, author, and ecologist (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_Bookchin).

Please find evidence of his death attached and reported by The Guardian: https://www.theguardian.com/news/2006/aug/08/guardianobituaries.usa

I am confident responsive records exist for this request, due to the FBI explicitly mentioning so in a response to a previous FOIA request pertaining to records mentioning the same subject (https://cdn.muckrock.com/foia_files/2020/03/12/E10e321976e7c230e26d58c00e902bd05bf6cb121_Q77394_R355480_D2446142.pdf). See the following, including relevant reference numbers to this request: 

"Records potentially responsive to your request were transferred to the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), and they were not previously processed pursuant to the FOIA.  You may file a request with NARA using the address above.  Please reference file numbers 100-HQ-454082 Serials 4, 6, 24, and 5; 100-HQ-454549 Serial 4-P17, 32, 42, 6-P16; 100-HQ-455596, 100-HQ-456482 Serial 9; 100-HQ-461197 Serial 13 and 2; 100-NY-166899, 62-HQ-117964 Serial 164, 88-HQ-49004 Serial 118, 76 89, 90, 91, 97, 77, 113, 145, 130, 186, and 166; 100-BS-46975 Serial 10; 100-BS-47199 Serial 1; and 100-AL-21998 Serial 435 in your correspondence."

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

J Ader

(90) calendar days, we will administratively close* only *the portion of
your case relating to 100-HQ-454082.



All of the remaining materials require screening for categories of
information exempted from disclosure under the terms of the FOIA, prior to
public release. In particular, there are documents that may be redacted to
protect the identities of confidential sources, including FBI informant
codes and informant file numbers.



Collectively, the responsive materials in your request amount to
approximately 235 pages. Requests for FBI case files that do not exceed 700

communications.subject: NARA Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Request Number RD 64052
communications.communication:
Dear J. Ader:

I completed processing the records you requested from the National Archives
and Records Administration under Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) tracking
number RD 64052.

You requested access to FBI/DOJ file numbers 100-HQ-454082 serials 4, 6,
24, and 5; 100-HQ-454549 serials 4-P17, 32, 42, 6-P16;
100-HQ-455596;100-HQ-456482 serial 9; 100-HQ-461197 serials 13 and 2;
100-NY-166899; 62-HQ-117964 serials 164; 88-HQ-49004 serials 76, 77, 89,
90, 91, 97, 113, 118, 145, 130, 166, and 186; 100-BS-46975; 100-BS-47199
serial 1; and 100-AL-21998 Serial 435 on Murray Bookchin.

In our initial March 2020 correspondence, you were informed that
62-HQ-117964 was not in our holdings and we only have serials 1-2 of
100-HQ-454082.

February 19, 2026 our office sent you an email informing you that
100-HQ-454549 serials 4 and 6; 100-HQ-455596;100-HQ-456482 serial 9;
100-HQ-461197 serials 13 and 2; 100-NY-166899; 100-BS-47199 serial 1;
100-AL-21998 Serial 435; and 100-BS-46975 serial 10 had been reviewed for
other requestors and were available for research.

I completed a line-by-line review of the remaining records you
requested. Please
be advised, I have considered the foreseeable harm standard when reviewing
records and applying FOIA exemptions for this request. Information was
released to the greatest extent possible. Below is a summary of my review:


Records Requested Total Pages Pages Released in Full Pages Released in
Part Pages
Withheld in Full
100-BS-46975 serials1-9 58 44 14 0
88-HQ-49004 serials 76-77  35 24 11 0
88-HQ-49004 serials 89-91 32 28 9 0
88-HQ-49004 serial 97 4 4 0 0
88-HQ-49004 serial 113 6 3 3 0
88-HQ-49004 serial 118 5 3 2 0
88-HQ-49004 serial 130 4 4 0 0
88-HQ-49004 serial 145 4 4 0 0
88-HQ-49004 serial 166 5 4 1 0
88-HQ-49004 serial 186 2 1 1 0

I withheld information protected under section (b) of the FOIA (5 U.S.C.
552). The specific reasons for the denials are:

TYPE OF INFORMATION WITHHELD

FOIA EXEMPTION or STATUTE

information exempted from disclosure by statute

the statute in support of this (b)(3) withholding is 5 USC 552 (b)(3),
pursuant to Rule 6(e) of the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure, which
preserves the secrecy of grand jury proceedings

(b)(3)

personal privacy of living individuals

(b)(6)

personal privacy of living individuals in law enforcement records

(b)(7)(C)

identities of confidential sources

(b)(7)(D)


You or your designated representative may view the file at the National
Archives at College Park, Maryland. We require at least one week advance
notice to prepare for your visit and ask that you email
specialaccess_foia@nara.gov with your FOIA tracking number (RD 64052) and
the date you plan to visit. Please monitor our web page
https://www.archives.gov/college-park for details and updates, as the
operating status for the facility could change, affecting opening hours for
the research rooms.


If you cannot visit our College Park facility, you may order a digital or
paper reproduction copy of the file at the cost of 80 cents per page. To
place a reproduction order, please forward this response to our office
email at specialaccess_foia@nara.gov or call 301-837-3190. A
mailing/billing address is required to generate a price quote, so please
include that information with your reproduction request.


It is possible the fees to hire a researcher may be less than the
reproduction fees. If you are unable to visit and you wish to hire a
researcher to duplicate the file, information on how to hire a researcher
can be found at this link: https://www.archives.gov/research/hire-help. The
National Archives does not endorse anyone who appears on the list.


If you are not satisfied with my action on this request, you have the right
to file an administrative appeal within ninety (90) calendar days from the
date of this letter. Appeals must be in writing and may be delivered by
regular U.S. mail or by email. By filing an appeal, you preserve your
rights under the Freedom of Information Act and present the deciding agency
with an opportunity to review your request and reconsider its decision. If
you submit your appeal by regular mail, it should be addressed to the
Deputy Archivist of the United States (ND), National Archives and Records
Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road, Room 4200, College Park, Maryland
20740-6001. Both the letter and envelope should be clearly marked “FOIA
Appeal.” If you submit your appeal by email, please send it to foia@nara.gov,
addressed to the Deputy Archivist, with the words “FOIA Appeal” in the
subject line. If you exercise your right to appeal, please explain why you
believe this response does not meet the requirements of the Freedom of
Information Act. All communications concerning this request should
reference your FOIA tracking number.

If you would like the opportunity to discuss my response and attempt to
resolve your dispute without initiating the appeals process, you may
contact our FOIA Public Liaison for assistance:

Accessioned Executive Branch Records – Washington, DC Area

FOIA Requester Service Center: 301-837-3190

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning or describing Justin Tanner Petersen AKA Agent Steal AKA Hydrerbad joker (28 July 1960 Washington, D.C. – 13 March 2010 Los Angeles, California), a hacker and informant for the Bureau. In an FBI affidavit, Petersen admitted to physically and electronically conducting illegal telephone taps and breaking into Pacific Bell's COSMOS and other companies' computer systems to check telephone numbers and determine the location of telephone lines and circuits.

Roughly 2700 pages of documentation has previously been released on Mr. Petersen, please exclude these documents from the search and provide a search of only unreleased documents. Mr. Petersen is DECEASED as of 2010 as the attached obituary from the LA times shows. Please release all reasonably segregable material which has not been previously released on this deceased subject.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Crose
